title: Support KB: Known issues landing page layout (filters, recency, escalate callouts) + troubleshooting readability guidelines
creator: Dev Patel
project: Customer Success & Support — Escalation playbook + Known-issues sprint (2026-02)
content:
## Context
Support is running a known-issues sprint to publish the highest-impact workarounds and link them consistently from Support workflows (Jira macros, triage checklist, escalation playbook). We need a docs landing page that:
- makes known issues findable fast (filtering + search)
- communicates freshness/recency clearly
- standardizes a prominent “When to escalate” callout per issue
- improves readability/scannability for troubleshooting content

This ticket is for design/content design guidance that unblocks ENG-4826 (implementation) and PR(s) in redwood-docs.

## Goals (what good looks like)
1) A Support-friendly landing page that works as the canonical hub (Support and CS can send customers here when appropriate).
2) Fast discovery: within ~30 seconds a Support agent can narrow to the relevant issue by tier + region/model + symptom category.
3) Strong guardrails: the page should steer users to escalation paths when workarounds don’t apply (and avoid implying guarantees).
4) Consistent article layout guidance: each workaround article reads like a runbook-lite (symptoms → impact → workaround → verification → escalate).

## Non-goals
- Redesigning the entire docs IA or migrating content systems.
- Creating net-new component library work beyond existing docs components.

## Proposed landing page layout (v1)
### Page header
- Title: “Known issues & workarounds”
- Subtitle: “Production-impacting issues we’re actively tracking, with validated workarounds when available.”
- Brief disclaimer: “Workarounds are temporary. If you’re blocked or impact is severe, follow the escalation guidance in each article.”

### Above-the-fold controls
1) Search input (site-level search is fine; add page-local filterable search if available)
2) Filter row (chips / dropdowns; responsive)
   - Tier: Hosted API | Dedicated | Private
   - Category (primary): Streaming | Quotas & rate limits | Autoscaling/capacity | Private installer/upgrades | Audit logs | Auth/SSO | Other
   - Region (optional, but high-value for Support): us-east | us-west | eu-west | ap-southeast | …
   - Model (optional): show only when article metadata has model tag(s)
   - “Show resolved” toggle (default off)
3) Sort control
   - Default: “Most recently updated”
   - Alternate: “Most viewed” (future; requires analytics) / “Alphabetical” (optional)

### Results list
- Card/list row per issue with:
  - Issue title (plain language)
  - 1-line symptom summary (e.g., “Streaming resets mid-generation; client sees truncated output.”)
  - Tag pills: Tier, Category, Region(s), Model(s) (truncate after 3–4 pills with “+N”)
  - Recency: “Updated YYYY-MM-DD” (required) + “First published YYYY-MM-DD” (optional)
  - Status badge: Investigating | Mitigation available | Fix rolling out | Monitoring | Resolved
  - Prominent “Escalate if…” micro-callout (single line) pulled from article metadata (see below)

### “Escalate” callout behavior (landing)
- Each card includes a one-liner “Escalate if:” with the highest-signal trigger (examples):
  - “Escalate if resets persist after retry/backoff and affect multiple users or P0 workflows.”
  - “Escalate if 429s occur below documented quota or headers are inconsistent across requests.”
- Clicking “Escalate if” anchors users to the “When to escalate” section inside the article.
- Secondary link: “Escalation playbook” (internal) / “Contact support” (external) depending on audience.

### Empty and error states
- If filters return none: “No known issues match these filters. If you’re seeing an outage or severe impact, contact Support and include request IDs + region + model.”

## Metadata requirements (to enable filtering + callouts)
To make filters work without manual curation, each known-issue article should expose frontmatter/metadata (or a JSON index) with:
- title
- slug/url
- tier: hosted|dedicated|private
- categories: [streaming, quotas, autoscaling, private-installer, audit-logs, auth]
- regions: [us-east, eu-west] (optional)
- models: [model-id] (optional)
- updated_at (required)
- status (required)
- escalate_blurb (required; <= 120 chars preferred)

ENG should confirm implementation approach (Docusaurus frontmatter vs separate index file). Design assumes URL parameters for shareable filtered views (e.g., ?tier=private&category=private-installer).

## Troubleshooting readability guidelines (article template)
Standard structure and visual hierarchy:
1) **Summary** (1–2 sentences)
2) **Symptoms** (bulleted; include exact error strings when safe)
3) **Impact** (what breaks; whether data loss risk)
4) **Affected**
   - Tiers
   - Regions
   - Models
   - SDK versions (if relevant)
5) **Workaround** (numbered steps; copy/paste-ready)
6) **Verification** (how to confirm mitigation worked; what metrics/logs to check)
7) **When to escalate** (explicit triggers; include “What to send Support” checklist)
8) **Related** (links: status page event, incident postmortem if shareable, relevant SDK troubleshooting section)

Component guidance:
- Use a consistent callout style for “When to escalate” (high contrast, not the same as “Note”).
- Use code blocks for headers/sample commands; avoid long paragraphs.
- Put safety/irreversibility warnings in a dedicated “Warning” callout.
- Accessibility: ensure color badges meet contrast; don’t rely only on color for status.

## Open questions
- Audience: Is this landing page public, or internal-only with a public subset?
  - Proposal: single page with “public” default; internal users see additional tags/articles via auth (if supported). If not supported, maintain two indexes.
- Do we need a severity indicator on the landing (P0–P4 / Sev mapping) or keep it implicit via “Escalate if” + status? Proposal: do NOT show P0–P4 publicly; keep internal-only to avoid contractual interpretation issues.

## Acceptance criteria
- Figma wireframe + redlines for desktop and mobile
- Final component behavior notes for filters, sorting, chips truncation, and recency display
- Copy blocks for:
  - landing subtitle/disclaimer
  - empty state
  - card “Escalate if” pattern
- Article readability checklist to include in publishing checklist (Docs/Support)

## Links
- ENG-4826 (implementation): known-issues landing + tagging + cross-links
- PM-913 (publication criteria)
- Confluence: Known issues index + sprint plan (internal)
comments: 2026-02-06 — Dev Patel: Support needs (1) tier + region filters, (2) very obvious recency, and (3) a one-line ‘when to escalate’ on the index so agents don’t have to click into every article during triage. Please keep the landing scannable; we’ll link this from Jira macros and intake checklist.
2026-02-07 — Priya Shah: +1 on recency. Also ask: can we support URL parameters so we can paste a filtered view into Slack bridges (e.g., ‘streaming + us-east’)?

2026-02-09 — Wei Chen: Proposed article outline looks good. Request: make the ‘What to send Support’ checklist a standard subsection under ‘When to escalate’ to reduce back-and-forth (request IDs, region, model, SDK version, timestamps).

2026-02-10 — Kira Thompson: For Private issues, please include a small ‘Safety’ warning pattern (rollback/migrations) so it stands out. Also suggest a “Resolved” toggle for Support to reference historical issues without cluttering default view.

2026-02-11 — Benji Okafor: Implementation note: easiest path is Docusaurus frontmatter + generated index. URL params are doable if we keep to a small set of filter keys. Please avoid requiring multi-select on v1; adds complexity.

2026-02-12 — Naomi Feldman: Please avoid exposing internal severity labels publicly. ‘Escalate if’ language should be customer-safe and should not include customer names, internal incident IDs, or hard promises on timelines.

2026-02-13 — Lena Morozov: Posted final spec in Figma (link in ENG ticket). Kept v1 filter set to Tier + Category + Region; Model/SDK are secondary tags shown on cards but not primary filters (can be revisited). Added clear ‘Updated’ date on every card and a standard ‘Escalate if’ micro-callout that deep-links to the article section.
